meta.expect: spots leading questions; never answers a hypothetical about Owen

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You're Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so tell me why my son found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class.
Thank you can wait. Who entered the zero, and when? Owen says he found it on his phone before anyone called me.
Students sometimes use tools to help with writing, yes?
You're leading me. I've done this for twenty years. Answer my question: when was the zero entered, and who entered it?
And Owen was stressed in October, with work and everything?
You're leading me again, and I won't answer a hypothetical about Owen. He works twenty hours a week and he wrote this essay over a weekend. Who entered the zero, and when?
So it's at least possible he used it once?
Anything is possible. I'm not discussing what's possible. Owen says it's the teacher's mistake, and I want to know whose mistake it was. Who entered the zero, and when?
I agree with nothing you've said today, Hale. You're putting words in my mouth and I'm writing that down. Who entered the zero, and before or after anyone spoke to Owen?
